page.summary: Deny the hook the Killer is actually carrying toward, early enough to force a drop or longer route; a broken hook alone is not a save.

verdict.recommendation: Read the likely hook and alternate route before spending sabotage time or charges.
verdict.soloQ: Attempt only a nearby, readable carry route; do not assume the carried teammate will escape simply because one hook breaks.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Call the target hook and whether a second player can cover the route; keep other teammates on objectives.
verdict.mainWeakness: The Killer can choose a different hook, hit the saboteur or leave the Survivor down.

options.whyItsHere: During another Survivor's carry, it reveals hooks within 56 m of the original pickup location and permits faster toolboxless sabotage; using that ability starts a 70/65/60-second cooldown.

opening: Use pickup position and nearby hooks to decide whether denying one hook can actually change the carry; ordinary sabotage is also possible with a suitable Toolbox, but none is assumed here.

rows.situation: The Killer picks up a teammate and the carry route is still undecided.
rows.action: Read the revealed hook positions around the original pickup and identify the hook the Killer can reach, including a plausible alternate.
rows.why: Saboteur shows normal hooks in white and Scourge Hooks in yellow during the carry; the auras are information, not a guarantee of route choice.

rows.situation: You are ahead of the carry at its intended hook and can sabotage before the Killer arrives.
rows.action: Break that hook without a Toolbox only if the changed route can matter and you have a safe exit after the action.
rows.why: The toolboxless action uses Saboteur's speed benefit and starts its cooldown; a late break or nearby alternate hook wastes the commitment.

rows.situation: The Killer takes another hook, hits you, drops the carried player or reaches the hook first.
rows.action: Stop chasing the old hook. Avoid a second down and switch to the next objective, recovery or rescue decision.
rows.why: Hook denial works through route pressure, not by forcing the Killer to keep carrying through a denied path.

abortWhen: The Killer has an uncontested alternate hook or reaches the target before sabotage completes.
The Killer turns to hit the saboteur or drops the carried Survivor.

weaknesses: The saboteur must be ahead of a moving carry and remains vulnerable near the Killer; one removed hook may not change the result.
commonMistakes: Breaking a convenient hook instead of the one on the active carry route.
Remaining near the Killer after the carry route changes or the teammate is dropped.
